name: Floor area ratio
seoDesc: Floor area ratio: work out carpet area from number of units and the indoor area. A free construction calculator with the formula, units and a worked example.
summary: Supply number of units, the indoor area, the walls area and the common area and the Floor area ratio calculator solves for carpet area. It is built for a materials order or a planning estimate you want to get roughly right first time. The panel waits for the button. Edit a field, press Calculate, and compare — one input at a time is enough to see what drives the answer.

sections.title: How does the Floor area ratio calculator work?
sections.html:
The Floor area ratio calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports carpet area in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you type in number of units, the indoor area, the walls area and the common area.

Press Calculate and the page works through the equation with the values you supplied and derives the rest; it then keeps up with you as you correct a typo.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the Floor area ratio calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Carpet area=indoor area − walls area
Built-up area=carpet area + walls area
Built-up area=total built-up area ÷ number of units
Built-up area=carpet area ÷ carpet to built-up area ratio
Super built-up area=built-up area + common area ÷ number of units
Super built-up area=carpet area × (loading factor (LF) + 1)

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

If a number looks wrong, check three things in this order: that the units match what you had in mind, that no drop-down is still on its default, and that the value you entered is on the same scale as the rest — a rate typed as 5 rather than 0.05 is the classic mistake. Those three account for almost every answer that is out by a factor.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Every quantity with units carries a chip beside its box. Switching the chip does not change what you know, only how it is written: values are converted to a common internal base, the arithmetic happens there, and the answer is converted back for display. Mixing metres with feet in one calculation is therefore safe.

Results are rounded for display but computed at full precision, so chaining one result into the next does not accumulate error. Very large and very small numbers switch to scientific notation rather than printing a run of zeros.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Floor area ratio calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Quoting a job where areas and quantities drive the price
  • Ordering material and not wanting a second trip
  • Checking a supplier's figure against your own measurements
  • Any time the same 4 figures keep coming back — number of units, the indoor area and the walls area — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.
  • Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.
  • Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the Floor area ratio calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns carpet area, derived from number of units, the indoor area and the walls area. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Floor area ratio calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for number of units, the indoor area, the walls area and the common area, which is 6 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter carpet area in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Carpet area opens in square meters and the chip beside it offers 24 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: Is the Floor area ratio calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — press Calculate and every result updates together.
